slides.texte_overlay:
How To Stop Being
Socially Afraid
Arrive early to events. It's much easier to talk to three people in a quiet room than to walk into a full one. Early arrivals become the hosts.
Prepare one opening line. "How do you know the host?" works almost everywhere. A ready sentence removes the panic of the first ten seconds.
Remember that awkward moments pass fast. You'll forget them in a week, and so will everyone else. Nothing you say is as big as it feels.
Join something with a shared activity. A climbing gym, a running club, a cooking class. Doing something together makes talking much easier.
Before: I avoided conversations because I felt I had nothing to say. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and I feel ready.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I avoided conversations because I felt I had nothing to say. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I feel ready.

slides.texte_overlay: Breathe out slowly before you walk in. A long exhale calms your body in seconds. A calmer body makes it much easier to speak first.
Count small wins. One hello, one question, one new name, one smile. Fear shrinks every time you prove to yourself that nothing bad happened.
